statements.action_statement: No fixed release is available yet; update when Docker Hardened Images publishes one.
statements.status_notes: CVE-2025-45582: GNU tar through 1.35 follows a symbolic link created by one archive when a later archive is extracted into the same directory, so a second archive can write through a ../ link planted by the first and overwrite files outside the extraction directory: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2025-45582. GNU tar's maintainer first answered that this is documented behaviour, since the manual advises extracting each untrusted archive into an empty directory (https://lists.gnu.org/archive/html/bug-tar/2025-08/msg00012.html). Upstream has since changed tar to confine extraction to the target directory, and Red Hat rates the CVE Moderate and ships a backport of those upstream changes as its fix (RHSA-2026:0002 for RHEL 10, with RHEL 8 and 9 updates; https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/cve-2025-45582; its tar.spec changelog reads Backport upstream changes to jailify extraction directory ... Fixes CVE-2025-45582: https://gitlab.com/redhat/centos-stream/rpms/tar/-/blob/c10s/tar.spec). No GNU tar release contains that change yet, so this is a fix still to be backported, not a dispute. The only build of this owner published in the DHI Alpine 3.24 repository is 1.35-r5, for x86_64 and aarch64, built from Alpine's tar 1.35-r5 recipe, which builds GNU tar 1.35 with a single patch (ignore-apk-tools-checksums.patch) that does not touch this code: https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/a9e2a2dc46f377eb25884f7fea9834492de7f518/main/tar/APKBUILD. Every published build is affected. Until a fix ships, extract each untrusted archive into a new empty directory.

GNU tar's maintainer first answered that this is documented behaviour, since the manual advises extracting each untrusted archive into an empty directory (https://lists.gnu.org/archive/html/bug-tar/2025-08/msg00012.html). Every build of this owner published in the DHI Debian repository, three rebuilds of Debian's tar 1.35+dfsg-3.1 for amd64 and arm64, is built from that Debian source, which does not contain the change.
